newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias unit seeks to sell sugar stocks.
newsitem.headline: Victorias unit seeks to sell sugar stocks.

text.p: The marketing arm of cash-strapped Victorias Milling Corp has asked approval from the Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) to sell in the domestic market an additional 500,000 bags (in 50-kg each) of refined sugar, SRA administrator Wilson Gamboa said on Tuesday.
North Negros Marketing Corp asked approval from the SRA to dispose in the domestic market an additional 500,000 bags of refined sugar, Gamboa said in a phone interview with Reuters.
Victorias Milling is seeking a moratorium on debts of 4.4 billion pesos.
In October 1996, the SRA also approved a separate application by North Negros to sell 500,000 bags of refined sugar.

"The application to sell additional sugar to the domestic market has been approved, but I witheld its release immediately in the market until they (North Negros) dispose stocks applied for last October," Gamboa said.
Gamboa said an inventory done by SRA recently showed that North Negros has so far disposed of 287,000 bags since it got approval last October.
"North Negros is oozing with sugar. These are all part of the raw sugar imported by the company in the past several months and refined by Victorias," Gamboa said.
Gamboa said the sugar has to be disposed off "because some of the stocks are now showing signs of deterioration."
"The company has incurred so much costs on the sugar in its warehouses in the past 10 months," he said.
The SRA regulates the sale of sugar.
